uniform_high_noise.description: Synthetic Erdos-Renyi camera-location recovery (n=100, p=0.5) under uniform random direction corruption with q=0.7 and noise sigma=0.2 (sigma times a random unit vector added to each clean unit direction, the authors' released generator), the setting of Supplement Table 14. Scored on 40 fixed hidden instances; the evaluator runs each registered solver on observations only.

median_location_error.description: Per-instance median camera error after L1 similarity alignment to ground truth (the paper's headline metric), averaged over instances; failed instances count at the error of the all-cameras-at-one-point output.

mean_location_error.description: Per-instance mean camera error after alignment, averaged over instances; catches methods that improve the median while leaving many cameras poor.

p90_location_error.description: Per-instance 90th-percentile camera error after alignment, averaged over instances; emphasises tail failures under heavy corruption.

uniform_high_noise._note: results hold the paper's Supplement Table 14 median errors (10 trials, the authors' implementation) for the annealing schedules lambda_t = t/(t+10) (cycle_sync), 10/(t+10) (reverse), 1 (cycle_only), t/(t+5) (fast) and 0 (cycle_sync_residual_only: residual-only reweighting inside the Cycle-Sync loop, T-AAB start). welsch_irls (the same residual-only reweighting from uniform weights) and lud (Least Unsquared Deviations by IRLS) are this gym's self-contained baselines; the paper reports no number for them in this setting. The paper reports only the median; mean and p90 are this gym's additional scored metrics. Up to the hardening pass the paper's lambda=0 number was attached to welsch_irls; it belongs to the lambda=0 ablation.

adversarial_high_noise.description: Synthetic Erdos-Renyi camera-location recovery (n=100, p=0.5) under cycle-consistent adversarial corruption (corrupted edges point along an alternative camera configuration) with q=0.45 and noise sigma=0.2 on every edge (the authors' released generator), the setting of Supplement Table 15. Scored on 40 fixed hidden instances; the evaluator runs each registered solver on observations only.
